The first --anchor reference run reported an unbalanced stack: 13294 is reached two pushes deep (JSR from 7B42, called from the walk). The stop's stack (FFEFF8) was declared for that exit.
A new synthetic case placed the pickup below its link and was rejected with 'trail owner unavailable'; the ordinary layout (link 0, pickup 1) was restored.
audit_world_writes still bounded frames by the pair capture's END (1066), which would have skipped the producer writes after it; it now uses the run's last loop.

Its evidence stopped with 'free slot 55 walked at 1067': P1's wrapper allocates a reversal effect into the shared pool before the loop, which the world evidence and the native world printer did not model. Both now do (a P1 birth printed first, then ordinary walks; logical owner 1). Rerun offline on that capture's artifacts, native then stopped at the session transport's 600-call cap ('mixed session invocation budget exhausted'); --world-session now allows 4096. With both fixes all 799 frames matched offline; the setup and joined captures were then rerun fresh because the evidence tool's hash changed.
